gp.heading: Gross profit
gp.text: Gross profit increased to $91.0 million and $265.1 million in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively. The increases in gross profit during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to increased revenues, partially offset by increased agent commissions, productivity awards, and other agent-related costs due to agent commission capping.

oi.heading: Operating Income (Loss)
oi.text: Operating income (loss), in the three months ended September 30, 2026, decreased when compared to the same period in 2025 primarily due to increased litigation expenses. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating income (loss) improved due to increased revenues and actions taken to reduce operating costs in the second half of 2025, partially offset by increased litigation expenses and accruals in connection with the Company’s ongoing efforts to resolve litigation matters, including the NAR settlement and other claims.

opex.text: Currently, our primary use of cash on hand is to sustain and grow our business operations, including, but not limited to, making commission and revenue share payments to agents and brokers and cash outflows for operating expenses, share repurchases, and dividend payments. In addition, the Company has no known material cash requirements as of September 30, 2026 relating to capital expenditures, commitments, or human capital (except as passthrough commissions to agents and brokers concurrent with settled real estate transactions), other than cash payments due pursuant to litigation settlement agreements, which may be paid in installments over time. For information regarding the Company’s expected cash requirement related to litigation settlement agreements, see Note 10 – Commitments and Contingencies to the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.

costs.text: Currently, our primary use of cash on hand is to sustain and grow our business operations, including, but not limited to, making commission and revenue share payments to agents and brokers and cash outflows for operating expenses, share repurchases, and dividend payments. In addition, the Company has no known material cash requirements as of September 30, 2026 relating to capital expenditures, commitments, or human capital (except as passthrough commissions to agents and brokers concurrent with settled real estate transactions), other than cash payments due pursuant to litigation settlement agreements, which may be paid in installments over time. For information regarding the Company’s expected cash requirement related to litigation settlement agreements, see Note 10 – Commitments and Contingencies to the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.

rd.heading: Technology and Development Expenses
rd.text: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, technology and development expenses increased compared to the same periods in 2025, primarily due to increased technology expenses related to agent support. These expenses include employee-related costs and other expenses for the maintenance and development of the technology used by both our agents and our employees.

sm.heading: Sales and Marketing Expenses
sm.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, sales and marketing expenses increased compared to the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, sales and marketing expenses decreased compared to the same period in 2025 due to efficiencies gained from our CRM of choice program in the U.S. and Canada residential real estate market.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, general and administrative expenses increased 6% and decreased 1%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025. The increase for the three months ended September 30, 2026 is primarily due to increased litigation expenses. The decrease for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 is primarily due to lower employee-related expenses, partially offset by increased litigation expenses. General and administrative expenses include costs related to wages, employee stock-based compensation, and other general overhead expenses.

nonint.text: Currently, our primary use of cash on hand is to sustain and grow our business operations, including, but not limited to, making commission and revenue share payments to agents and brokers and cash outflows for operating expenses, share repurchases, and dividend payments. In addition, the Company has no known material cash requirements as of September 30, 2026 relating to capital expenditures, commitments, or human capital (except as passthrough commissions to agents and brokers concurrent with settled real estate transactions), other than cash payments due pursuant to litigation settlement agreements, which may be paid in installments over time. For information regarding the Company’s expected cash requirement related to litigation settlement agreements, see Note 10 – Commitments and Contingencies to the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.

nonop.heading: Other (Income) Expense, Net
nonop.text: For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, total other (income) expense, net shifted to net other expense of $5,890 million and $5,087 million, respectively, from net other income of ($413) million and ($1,989) million for the same periods in 2025. The change was primarily due to losses on the sale and impairment of equity investments in 2026. Total other (income) expense, net includes interest income earned on cash and cash equivalents, and (earnings) losses related to equity investments.

tax.text: The Company’s provision for income taxes was an expense of $1.5 million and an expense of $0.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, which represented effective tax rates of (53.3%) and 21%, respectively. The expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by stock-based compensation shortfalls.

net.text: We define consolidated adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss), excluding other income (expense), net, income tax benefit (expense), depreciation, amortization, impairment charges, litigation contingency, legal costs non-recurring, stock-based compensation expense, stock option expense, and other items that are not core to the operating activities of the Company, as applicable. Segment adjusted EBITDA is defined consistently as segment net income (loss), excluding other income (expense), net, income tax benefit (expense), depreciation, amortization, impairment charges, litigation contingency, legal costs non-recurring, stock-based compensation expense, stock option expense, and other non-core items, as applicable. We believe these measures provide useful information to investors about our financial performance, help identify underlying trends that could otherwise be masked by excluded expenses, and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by management for financial and operational decision-making.

wc.heading: Net Working Capital
wc.text:
Net working capital is calculated as the Company’s total current assets less its total current liabilities. The following table presents our net working capital as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025:

As of September 30, 2026, net working capital increased by $24.8 million, compared to net working capital as of December 31, 2025 primarily due to an increase in restricted cash and net accounts receivable, as a result of the timing of receivable collections, as well as a decrease in the litigation contingency due to the payments made in June 2026.

capex.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cash used in investing activities decreased due to lower cash used for investments in affiliates and purchases of property and equipment, partially offset by increased cash used for the purchase of a business compared to the same period in 2025.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text: Revenues substantially represent the commission revenue earned by the Company for closed brokerage real estate transactions in addition to fees paid to the Company by agents. The Company’s revenues increased 6% and 7% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025, primarily due to higher home sales prices in North America, increased international production, and improved productivity in North America.

intro.text: Built by Agents. Built for Agents. AGNT, Inc. (Nasdaq: AGNT) is the global parent company of eXp Realty®, the most agent-centric™ real estate brokerage on the planet, NextHome, Inc., an award-winning national real estate franchise, FrameVR.io, a virtual collaboration platform, and SUCCESS® Enterprises, a leading personal development and media brand for entrepreneurs. Together, the AGNT platform provides a world-class multi-model operating system empowering independent agents, franchise owners, and team leaders across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia Pacific, and South Africa. As a publicly traded company, AGNT prioritizes transparency, innovation, and long-term value for agents, franchise owners, staff, and shareholders.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The North American Realty segment includes operations across all 50 U.S. states and all Canadian provinces and represented 96.9% of total consolidated revenues in 2025.

The International Realty segment includes operations in 27 countries throughout the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, and South Africa and represented 3.1% of total consolidated revenues in 2025.

For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 approximately 13 %, 11 % and 9 %, respectively, of the Company’s total revenue was generated outside of the U.S. Long-lived assets held outside of the U.S. were 10 % and 17 % as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

As noted in this Annual Report, the National Association of Realtors (“NAR”), and various Multiple Listing Service (“MLS”) systems are the primary source for third-party industry data and those systems generally state that the information contained therein has been obtained from sources believed to be reliable.

The Company also utilizes part-time and temporary employees and consultants when necessary; in a limited number of the Company’s foreign markets, the Company relies on the use of indirect employment structures where personnel providing certain services to the foreign entities are employed by a contractor of the Company and are not employed by the Company.
Fluctuations in housing inventory levels can negatively impact the Company’s business, which depends on the ability of its brokers and agents to facilitate home sales.
The Company depends on the industry experience and talent of its current executives.
In addition, the Company relies on third-party vendors to provide key components of the Company’s cloud office platform and to provide additional systems and related support.
The Company’s operations rely on the performance of real estate brokers and agents.
The Company also depends on access to MLSs in the Company’s markets, which serve as critical sources of property data and listing distribution.

The Company also assesses cybersecurity risks presented by key suppliers and service providers , document their security posture through internal tools, and in certain cases requires third party audit reports or contractual notification of security incidents.
